title: Embeddings throughput amplification and graceful backpressure
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our embeddings and reranking endpoints are showing intermittent latency spikes and long tail queueing under mixed small/large request patterns. Current autoscaler uses simple CPU/GPU utilization signals and a global queue depth threshold which leads to either overprovisioning for bursty tenants or underprovisioning for sustained high-throughput customers. We need a production-safe plan to increase end-to-end embedding throughput while providing graceful backpressure, predictable latency SLOs, and capacity forecasting for sales/ops.

Objectives:
- Increase steady-state embeddings throughput by at least 2x for common small-batch workloads via dynamic batching and per-shard batching optimizations.
- Provide queue-level backpressure and per-tenant rate limiting so slow bursts do not starve other tenants.
- Improve autoscaler decision quality by adding request-rate and pending-requests signals and implementing scale-up/down hysteresis tuned for embedding workloads.
- Surface capacity and estimated time-to-provision in Console for Dedicated customers and in internal dashboards for capacity planning.

Scope (in-scope): autoscaler signals & policy, request queue redesign (per-shard queue + priority tiers), per-tenant rate limiter, dynamic batching tuning, telemetry and SLO metrics, load tests and canary rollout.

Out of scope for this ticket: model quantization changes, major changes to reusable embedding model architectures, or downstream SDK changes (those will get follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: P95 embedding latency under a 50 RPS pattern with 1-4 vector batch sizes remains < 120ms in all regions for hosted customers
Autoscaler responds to 3x sustained request-rate increase within configured SLO window without causing >20% failed requests
Per-tenant rate limiting prevents single-tenant noisy neighbor incidents in mixed-load tests (verified by synthetic multi-tenant load test)
New metrics are visible in Console and internal Grafana: pending_requests_total (per-shard), dynamic_batch_size_distribution, per_tenant_rejections, autoscaler_scale_decision_reason
tasks: Infra: add per-shard pending-requests gauge and expose via /metrics (ENG-9160)
Runtime: implement priority-aware per-shard queues with fast-path for small batches
Runtime: dynamic batching optimizer that favors latency for small batches and throughput for large batches
Autoscaler: add request-rate and pending_requests signals, implement scale-up/down hysteresis and cooldown windows
API: add per-tenant token and request rate limiters with configurable tiers and backoff response codes
Observability: dashboard and alert for queue depth SLO breaches and per-tenant throttling
Testing: large-scale synthetic multi-tenant load test harness and 2-stage canary plan
Docs: runbook and Console doc for Dedicated capacity estimates
notes: Design trade-offs considered: local per-shard queueing reduces cross-shard head-of-line blocking but complicates uniform fairness across shards.
We discussed tokenization and embedding cost: small inputs dominate request count; dynamic batching must prioritize latency when batch size <= 4.
Potential regression: per-tenant rate limits could break clients that do large fanout; plan to add informative 429 body with a link to quota policy.
implementation_notes: Start with metric plumbing and load test harness to reproduce production patterns (Marcus & SRE) - week 1
Iterate on batching policy in a feature branch, expose an internal toggle to compare latency/throughput trade-offs
Autoscaler changes gated behind feature flag and rolled to one region with canary traffic routed by Console
Include a telemetry spike detector to avoid autoscaler oscillations during noisy bursts
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive batching increases P99 latency for latency-sensitive customers. Mitigation: latency-aware batching and per-route configuration.
Risk: new rate limiter could cause unexpected client errors. Mitigation: default to permissive thresholds in hosted, send warning headers and soft 429 with retry-after in initial rollout.
Risk: capacity forecast in Console might be misaligned with real provisioning lead times. Mitigation: couple forecast with real infra lead-time inputs and add confidence intervals.
testing_plan: Build multi-tenant synthetic load generator that can replay production traffic shapes
Run stress tests across regions with mixed small/large batch distributions and record latency/throughput metrics
Perform chaos tests: kill a shard during sustained load to validate graceful degradation and failover
Canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on SLO violations
